title: TikTok rolls out an AI shopping assistant and one-click checkout
key_facts: TikTok announced on Monday that it is launching an AI shopping assistant and a new in-app checkout feature that lets users buy directly from brands.

TikTok describes the Shopping Assistant as a conversational AI agent designed to help users discover and purchase products; it says the assistant understands context and remembers users' preferences and needs throughout the conversation.
The assistant offers real-time, AI-powered shopping guidance such as product details, shipping information, sizing, availability and help completing a purchase.
With the new checkout, users can buy directly from a brand from their For You feed (the app's main, algorithm-driven video feed) with one click.
TikTok says the features are being built with commerce platforms and payment providers including Salesforce, Shopify, Shoplazza and Stripe, among others.

TechCrunch's reading (not TikTok's): the features could let TikTok capture more of users' shopping journeys and potentially more transaction value, and TikTok appears to hope users stay in the app for product questions rather than turning to outside AI tools such as ChatGPT.

TikTok's Economic Impact Report, released last week, says activity on the platform helped generate $81 billion in GDP for US businesses, and 54 million Americans said they bought a product after watching a TikTok video.
TikTok Shop, the app's in-house marketplace, launched in the US in September 2023; eMarketer estimates it generated about $15.8 billion in US sales in 2025, roughly 18% of all US social commerce.
